title: Automated non-enhancing tumor segmentation gives a prognostic index in glioblastoma
summary: A deep learning model segmented enhancing tumor, edema and necrosis on MRI from 940 patients, and a finite mixture model isolated edema subregions containing non-contrast-enhancing tumor to compute a Diffuse Infiltration Index (DII). A high DII doubled the hazard of death in the NCT03439332 cohort (HR 2.09, 95% CI 1.34-3.25), with smaller effects in the other cohorts (pooled HR 1.28). Retrospective, and deep learning is only the segmentation step. Preprint of 2025-06-28.
ai_technology: Deep learning segmentation of enhancing tumor, edema and necrosis, followed by a non-local spatially varying finite mixture model

evidence.tested: Survival analysis across four multicenter cohorts (940 patients) with confirmation of smaller effects in other cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Surgical benefit of using DII and peer-reviewed status are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning segmentation supplied the regions from which the infiltration index was computed.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations were not available. Publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
